MUQATIL:63:9-11/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:63:9-11/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:63:9-11/r1.claim: The address calls those who acknowledge faith hypocrites; they must not let wealth and children distract them from obligatory prayer, since abandoning it makes them losers.

TUSTARI:63:9/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:63:9/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:63:9/r1.claim: Wealth and children must not distract from performing obligations on time; anyone diverted from God’s remembrance and service by worldly desire and then pleased with worship is deceived, except one God takes.

TUSTARI:63:9/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:63:9/r2.speaker: سلمان
TUSTARI:63:9/r2.claim: Salman said he did not weep from fear of death or greed for the world, but because the Prophet had instructed them to keep only a traveler’s provision; his possessions were modest bedding and utensils.

TUSTARI:63:9/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:63:9/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:63:9/r3.claim: The Prophet’s instruction was that one’s worldly provision should be no more than a traveler’s supplies.

TUSTARI:63:9/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:63:9/r4.speaker: سلمان
TUSTARI:63:9/r4.claim: Salman advised Saʿd to remember God when he intends, when he judges, and when he swears.

TAB-FULL:v22p670/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p670/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p670/r1.claim: Wealth and children must not cause believers to neglect remembrance of God; the verb means to distract or divert someone from something.

TAB-FULL:v22p670/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p670/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p670/r2.claim: The verb’s meaning is illustrated by Imruʾ al-Qays’s line about distracting a woman from her child with amulets.

TAB-FULL:v22p670/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p670/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v22p670/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets remembrance of God here specifically as the five daily prayers.

TAB-FULL:v22p673/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p673/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v22p673/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk describes a believer dying with wealth but unpaid zakat, unperformed Hajj, and unpaid dues to God; he asks to return, but death is not delayed.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3357#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3357#3/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3357#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits the Prophet's warning that a person able to perform pilgrimage or owing zakat who fails to act will ask to return at death; he supports it with this sura's warning about wealth and children distracting from God.

NAHHAS:v4p434/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p434/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p434/r15.claim: The command means wealth and children must not distract from God's remembrance; tulhikum derives from causing someone to forget and be distracted.

NAHHAS:v4p434/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p434/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p434/r16.claim: A poem uses alhaytuhā for distracting a nursing woman from her child; those who do this lose mercy and reward.

SULAMI:v2p329#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p329#2/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p329#2/r1.claim: Wealth and children must not distract from performing obligatory worship at its earliest time; any worldly attraction that diverts from remembrance and service brings loss.

THALABI:v9p323/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p323/r1.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v9p323/r1.claim: The commentators explain remembrance of God as the five daily prayers and compare 63:9 with 24:37.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r1.speaker: عطاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r1.claim: The remembrance from which wealth and children must not distract is prescribed prayer.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r2.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r2.claim: It means God's obligations, including prayer and other duties.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r3.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r3.claim: It means obeying God through jihad.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p18/r4.claim: It may mean fearing God when He is remembered.

QUSHAYRI:v3p321/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p321/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p321/r13.claim: Do not neglect religion for wealth or children: prioritize God's due and He will manage worldly needs; your obligation is to God, while He guarantees your provision.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p477/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p477/r1.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p477/r1.claim: Ata identifies remembrance of God as His obligations, including pilgrimage and almsgiving.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p477/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p477/r2.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p477/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies remembrance of God as the five daily prayers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p477/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p477/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p477/r3.claim: Muqatil identifies remembrance as the prescribed prayer and says this verse and the next address hypocrites who professed faith.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p477/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p477/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p477/r4.claim: The verse says that one who lets wealth and children distract him does so by his own action, since wealth itself does not distract someone who resists its temptation.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:63:9-11/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:63:9-11/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:63:9-11/r1.claim: Wealth and children must not distract from God's remembrance, meaning the five daily prayers; those distracted from prayer are losers.

JISHUMI:v10p6945/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6945/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6945/r8.claim: Anything that occupies someone and makes them neglect another matter has distracted them; wealth is named as the cause, as in expressions where an effect is attributed to its cause.

JISHUMI:v10p6945/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6945/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6945/r9.claim: The term ajal means a period or fixed term, while ājil is the opposite of immediate.

JISHUMI:v10p6946/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r5.claim: Dhikr of God here most aptly means all forms of obedience.

JISHUMI:v10p6946/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r6.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r6.claim: Another view restricts remembrance to the five daily prayers; other views take it as remembrance at all times or gratitude, patience, and acceptance in every condition.

JISHUMI:v10p6946/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r7.claim: One should not neglect God in hardship or blessing, since His beneficence continues in every condition.

JISHUMI:v10p6946/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6946/r8.claim: Those distracted lose God's reward and mercy.

JISHUMI:v10p6948/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6948/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6948/r4.claim: The command not to let wealth distract people shows that their acts originate from them; otherwise it would be God distracting them, and the text also says they are the losers.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p134/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p134/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p134/r1.claim: Wealth and children must not distract from remembrance, meaning the five prayers; compare those not distracted by trade.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p134/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p134/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p134/r2.claim: Whoever is distracted from remembrance by wealth and children is a loser.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p545#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p545#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p545#2/r1.claim: Wealth distracts through its management, pursuit of growth and profit, trade, and enjoyment; children distract through affection, care, and providing for their needs during life and after one's death.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p545#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p545#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p545#2/r2.claim: Believers already know that wealth and children are slight beside what God has, so remembrance of God must take precedence over them.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p545#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p545#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p545#2/r3.claim: Being occupied with worldly life at the expense of religion makes people lose their trade by exchanging the lasting good for a paltry, passing thing.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p545#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p545#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p545#2/r4.claim: One interpretation identifies remembrance of God with the five daily prayers.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p545#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p545#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p545#2/r5.claim: Al-Hasan interprets remembrance as all religious duties, effectively obedience to God.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p545#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p545#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p545#2/r6.claim: Another interpretation identifies remembrance with the Qur'an.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p545#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p545#2/r7.speaker: الكلبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p545#2/r7.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets remembrance as fighting alongside the Messenger of God.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#2/r1.claim: Ilhāʾ is distraction through pleasure and appetite; remembrance of God includes prayer, monotheism, supplication, and every obligatory or recommended act, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya considers the stronger view over limiting it to prescribed prayer.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك وعطاء وأصحابه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p315#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, ʿAṭāʾ, and their companions limit remembrance here to the prescribed prayer.

TABRISI:63:11#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:63:11#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:63:11#2/r3.claim: Wealth and children must not distract believers from the five prescribed prayers.

TABRISI:63:11#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:63:11#2/r4.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:63:11#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, remembrance of God covers all forms of obedience.

TABRISI:63:11#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:63:11#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:63:11#2/r5.claim: Another interpretation is remembering God's gifts with gratitude, meeting affliction with patience, and accepting His decree, in both hardship and blessing.

TABRISI:63:11#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:63:11#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:63:11#2/r6.claim: Whoever is distracted by wealth or children loses God's reward and mercy.

TABRISI:63:11/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:63:11/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:63:11/r7.claim: Infidād means dispersal; silver is named for its distribution in the prices of purchased things, and anything distracting one from another thing is called a diversion.

TABRISI:63:11/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:63:11/r8.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
TABRISI:63:11/r8.claim: His line about a poem distracting the sons of Jusham from every virtue supplies an example of the verb ‘to distract.’

TABRISI:63:11/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:63:11/r9.speaker: امرؤ القيس
TABRISI:63:11/r9.claim: His line about distracting a pregnant woman and nursing mother also witnesses the meaning of ‘to distract.’

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#2/r1.claim: The prohibition means that wealth and children must not distract believers.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#2/r2.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#2/r2.claim: Here remembrance of God means obeying Him in jihad.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#2/r3.speaker: عطاء ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#2/r3.claim: Here remembrance of God means the obligatory prayer.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#2/r4.claim: Here remembrance means the obligatory duties, including prayer and other obligations.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p277#2/r5.claim: The phrase is general, urging believers to persist in remembrance of God.

RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r1.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r1.claim: Commentators disagree whether the warning about being distracted by wealth and children addresses hypocrites or believers; Muqātil says this verse and those after it address hypocrites who professed faith.

RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r2.claim: The phrase means do not let wealth and children occupy you, as they occupied the hypocrites.

RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r3.claim: Dhikr of God is interpreted as God's duties such as prayer, zakat, and pilgrimage, or as obedience to God; al-Ḍaḥḥāk specifies the five prayers.

RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk specifically identifies remembrance of God here with the five prescribed prayers.

RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r5.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r5.claim: Muqātil says this verse and what follows address hypocrites who had professed faith.

RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r6.claim: The losers exchange what is noble and lasting for what is base and temporary; alternatively, they lose by denying the Messenger's claims of oneness and resurrection.

RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r7.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r7.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies another form of remembrance from which wealth must not distract as fighting in God's cause.

RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p17#2/r8.claim: Other interpretations identify remembrance as the Qurʾān itself or reflecting and pondering over it.

RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p18/r4.claim: The warning about wealth and children calls for remembrance before death; the order to spend calls for gratitude for what God provided.

QURTUBI-FULL:63:9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:63:9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:63:9/r1.claim: Believers are warned against the hypocrites' habits: those hypocrites withheld their wealth and urged others not to spend on the Messenger's companions.

QURTUBI-FULL:63:9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:63:9/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:63:9/r2.claim: The remembrance from which wealth distracts may mean Hajj and zakat, Quran recitation, or continual remembrance.

QURTUBI-FULL:63:9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:63:9/r3.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:63:9/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the remembrance means the five prescribed prayers.

QURTUBI-FULL:63:9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:63:9/r4.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:63:9/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says it means all obligations, equivalent to saying obedience to God.

QURTUBI-FULL:63:9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:63:9/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:63:9/r5.claim: Another view takes the address as directed to hypocrites: they professed faith, so they should believe inwardly as well.

QURTUBI-FULL:63:9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:63:9/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:63:9/r6.claim: Anyone distracted by property and children from obedience to the Lord is among the losers.

BAYDAWI-FULL:63:8-10/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:63:8-10/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:63:8-10/r2.claim: Wealth and children distract through their management and attention from prayer and other worship that recalls God; addressing the possessions directly heightens the prohibition.

BAYDAWI-FULL:63:8-10/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:63:8-10/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:63:8-10/r3.claim: Anyone diverted by possessions is a loser, having traded the lasting great good for a paltry, transient thing.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p249#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p249#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p249#4/r1.claim: Wealth and children should not distract from the five prayers or Qur'an; their management, increase, affection, and care can occupy people.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p249#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p249#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p249#4/r2.claim: Another interpretation is to become busy investing wealth instead of managing one's afterlife, or pleasing children instead of preparing for return to God.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p249#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p249#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p249#4/r3.claim: Such people lose their trade by selling the enduring for the transient.

QASHANI:63:9-11/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:63:9-11/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:63:9-11/r1.claim: Sincere faith makes love of God outweigh love of family and wealth; otherwise attachments veil believers, waste their innate light, and lead to loss.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r2.claim: Money distracts through pursuit of increase and enjoyment of accumulation; children distract through delight and concern for their interests. Remembrance broadly includes prayer, praise, glorification, and supplication.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r3.speaker: الضحاك وعطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and ʿAṭāʾ restrict remembrance to obligatory prayer; al-Ḥasan also says all duties, al-Kalbī says jihad with the Messenger, and another view says Qurʾān.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p184/r4.claim: Those distracted by wealth and children lose by choosing the immediate over the later and the perishable over the lasting.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p133/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p133/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p133/r1.claim: Believers are urged to remember God abundantly and not let wealth or children distract them; whoever is absorbed by worldly adornment instead of obedience loses himself and his family at Resurrection.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p133/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p133/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p133/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says someone with means for Hajj or liable zakat who neglects it will ask to return at death; he gives two hundred as the zakat threshold and provisions plus a mount for Hajj.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p614/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p614/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p614/r1.claim: Wealth and children must not absorb the heart through their care or enjoyment and distract it from remembering God.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p614/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p614/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p614/r2.claim: Remembering God includes every act of religion; it prevents believers from repeating the hypocrites’ calls to withhold money or expel the weaker party.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p614/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p614/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p614/r3.claim: The verse rhetorically addresses wealth and children while intending to forbid people themselves from being distracted by them.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p614/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p614/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p614/r4.claim: Those who persist in distraction are the true losers, contrary to their aim of increasing and preserving their worldly holdings.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p614/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p614/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p614/r5.claim: Whoever gives religious duties priority can entrust worldly needs to God, who provides for and protects the servant devoted to Him.

DURR-FULL:v8p179/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r1.claim: The Prophet says righteous members of his community are not distracted by trade or sale from remembering God and performing the five obligatory prayers.

DURR-FULL:v8p179/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r2.claim: The Prophet says a person able to perform pilgrimage or owing zakat who neglects it will ask to return at death; Ibn Abbas supports the warning by reciting the whole surah.

DURR-FULL:v8p179/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says a dying believer who withheld zakat, pilgrimage dues, or another due to God will ask to return and give charity and zakat; God will not delay the appointed term.

DURR-FULL:v8p179/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r4.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says remembrance means the five prayers, while spending from one's provision means zakat and expenditure for pilgrimage.

DURR-FULL:v8p179/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r5.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v8p179/r5.claim: Ata identifies remembrance of God here with the obligatory prayer.

BURSEVI:v9p436#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p436#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p436#2/r2.claim: Lahiya means to forget, neglect, or turn away; lahw also means play. Wealth and children must not divert believers from prayer and other acts that recall God.

BURSEVI:v9p436#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p436#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v9p436#2/r3.claim: Remembrance includes fear of God in the heart; Qur’an recitation and religious learning by tongue; and prayer and other obedience by the body.

BURSEVI:v9p436#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p436#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p436#2/r4.claim: The warning concerns leaving remembrance because of worldly preoccupation; naming the cause instead of its effect intensifies the rebuke.

BURSEVI:v9p436#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p436#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v9p436#2/r5.claim: A rhetorical alternative calls the wording metonymy: moving from ‘do not let them distract you’ to ‘do not be distracted’ shifts from a necessary cause to its result.

BURSEVI:v9p436#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p436#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p436#2/r6.claim: Hypocrites were miserly and proud of their children and clans, occupied with them instead of God, obedience, and supporting His Messenger.

BURSEVI:v9p436#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p436#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p436#2/r7.claim: Anyone distracted by worldly life from religion, even briefly, is fully lost, having sold the lasting and great for the petty and transient.

BURSEVI:v9p437/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p437/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p437/r1.claim: A Persian verse continued from the preceding discussion says the speaker has closed the heart to the delights of both worlds and wants only God.

BURSEVI:v9p437/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p437/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p437/r2.claim: A report says two angels call at sunrise that a little which suffices is better than much that distracts; all creatures except humans and jinn hear them.

BURSEVI:v9p437/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p437/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p437/r3.claim: For perfected people of witnessing faith, even seeing their good deeds or spiritual unveilings must not distract from God’s essence, attributes, Names, or manifestation in deeds and states.

BURSEVI:v9p437/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p437/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p437/r4.claim: Turning from the Benefactor to created things and their gifts loses spiritual capital and veils the true Witness; the firmly established are protected while the weak remain immersed in worldly concerns.

BURSEVI:v9p437/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p437/r5.speaker: سهل
BURSEVI:v9p437/r5.claim: Sahl says wealth and children must not delay obligations from their earliest appointed times; whoever is diverted from remembrance and service by worldly goods is a loser.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r1.claim: Do not let attention to managing, benefiting from, and enjoying wealth and children distract from prayer and other acts that recall the true object of worship.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r10.claim: They are losers because they exchanged enduring, great gain for something fleeting and contemptible; the definite wording, demonstrative, restriction, and repeated attribution intensify the claim.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r11.claim: The warning prepares for the following general order to spend, countering the hypocrites' call to stop supporting the Messenger.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r2.speaker: الحسن وجماعة
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan and others take remembrance of God as a metonym for all worship, since worship causes remembrance and remembrance is its true aim.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r3.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r3.claim: A report from al-Ḥasan takes remembrance to mean all obligatory duties.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r4.speaker: الضحاك، عطاء
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and ʿAṭāʾ say remembrance here means the obligatory prayer.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r5.speaker: الكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r5.claim: Al-Kalbī interprets remembrance as fighting alongside the Messenger.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers the general interpretation of remembrance as worship.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r7.speaker: الكشاف
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r7.claim: Al-Kashshāf understands wealth and children as worldly life generally, since they are its most coveted parts, citing the verse that calls wealth and sons worldly adornment.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r8.claim: The prohibition is directed at the believers, but is attributed to wealth and children as if they themselves distract, because of their strong causal role; this is an attributional or causal figure.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p117/r9.claim: The warning means being occupied with wealth and children; this is more forceful than simply saying “whoever is distracted by them.”

ELMALILI:63:9-11/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r1.claim: The address is to sincere believers seeking the divine honor granted to believers.

ELMALILI:63:9-11/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r2.claim: The cares of wealth and children must not distract believers from remembering God; the verse does not command abandoning these responsibilities.

ELMALILI:63:9-11/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r3.claim: “God’s remembrance” includes prayer and other obligatory and voluntary worship that recalls God’s names, attributes, commands, reward, and punishment and trains people to act for Him.

ELMALILI:63:9-11/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r4.claim: The worship includes congregational prayer, fasting, almsgiving, pilgrimage, struggle, Qur’an recitation, preaching, and acts of glorification and praise.

ELMALILI:63:9-11/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r5.claim: Whoever lets wealth and children cause forgetfulness of God is a loser who traded the everlasting for the fleeting and loses lasting honor.

ELMALILI:63:9-11/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:63:9-11/r6.claim: Elmalılı links the warning to the verse that calls wealth and children worldly adornment and lasting good deeds better with God.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p250/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p250/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p250/r5.claim: The discourse turns from exposing hypocrites to urging believers not to be distracted and to spend for good and communal needs, countering the order not to support the Prophet’s followers.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r1.claim: Working for wealth and children is not blameworthy when it does not distract from God’s remembrance; such distraction has degrees.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r2.speaker: علماء أصول الفقه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r2.claim: The warning that whoever does this is a loser supports the legal principle that a prohibition requires refraining from the act.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r3.claim: “That” means being distracted by wealth and children: abandoning required remembrance such as prayer on time and failing to observe divine commands and prohibitions.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r4.claim: Distraction by anything other than wealth or children is even more deserving of the prohibition and warning.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251#2/r5.claim: The separating pronoun rhetorically restricts “the losers” to those who disobey, exaggerating their loss; the demonstrative says they deserve that outcome.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251/r1.claim: Addressing believers through the relative clause signals concern that they obey the prohibition.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251/r2.claim: Wealth and children are singled out because wealth absorbs time in acquisition and growth, and its accumulation can displace remembrance of the duty to give.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251/r3.claim: Care for children, managing their needs, and enjoying their company can also distract from remembering divine commands and prohibitions.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251/r4.claim: The wording addresses wealth and children as the distractors but means their owners; the following “whoever does that” confirms this causal rhetorical construction.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251/r5.claim: The second lā is a coordinating negative before “your children”; since prohibition implies negation, it reinforces the ban on being occupied by children as strongly as by wealth.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p251/r6.claim: Dhikr includes both spoken remembrance such as prayer and Quran recitation, and inward recollection through reflection on God and obedience; ʿUmar calls the latter superior at commands and prohibitions.

TABATABAI:63:9-11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:63:9-11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:63:9-11/r1.claim: The passage warns believers away from traits that cause hypocrisy, especially distraction by wealth and children and miserliness.

TABATABAI:63:9-11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:63:9-11/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:63:9-11/r2.claim: Ilhāʾ means occupying or distracting; wealth and children distract when attachment to them as worldly adornment turns the heart away from God.

TABATABAI:63:9-11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:63:9-11/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:63:9-11/r3.claim: Attachment empties the heart of remembrance, leaving only verbal profession without action or inward belief; when servants forget God, He forgets them, bringing clear loss.

TABATABAI:63:9-11/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:63:9-11/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:63:9-11/r4.claim: The loss is like the hypocrites who traded guidance for error and gained nothing; the author links this to 2:16.

TABATABAI:63:9-11/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:63:9-11/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:63:9-11/r5.claim: The verse indirectly but emphatically forbids attachment: instead of merely warning believers not to be distracted, it treats wealth and children as having a distracting nature.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p329/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p329/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p329/r6.claim: The closing three verses warn Muslims not to let wealth and children distract from remembering God; those who fail to spend for God's cause will regret it after death, when regret is useless.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p329/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p329/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p329/r7.claim: The first section identifies worldly love as the root of hypocrisy; the second urges Muslims to guard against that same cause.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p337/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p337/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p337/r2.claim: Muslims are warned not to copy hypocrites whose love of wealth and children makes them forget God and the Hereafter, which is true loss and Satan’s faction.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:63:9/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:63:9/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:63:9/r1.claim: The warning does not require neglecting family or work; ordinary care and earning are natural, but they must not obscure life's meaning or awareness of serving God.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:63:9/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:63:9/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:63:9/r2.claim: If worldly preoccupations overwhelm someone, they may postpone duties while assuming life is long; when death arrives, the test is over and they beg for more time.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p178/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p178/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p178/r1.claim: The warning concerns managing and growing wealth or attending to children until one neglects God's remembrance and prefers them over Him; such a person suffers immense loss.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p179/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p179/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p179/r1.claim: Ilha means distracting, unlike ordinary occupation, which can be praiseworthy, as prayer is described as an occupation and Paradise's people are joyfully occupied; the stronger blameworthy word best suits the warning.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p179/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p179/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p179/r2.claim: The grammar makes wealth and children the agents forbidden to distract, while believers are the intended people being warned against becoming preoccupied with them.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p179/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p179/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p179/r3.claim: The rhetorical shift parallels the warning that worldly life and the Deceiver not delude people: the apparent target is the cause, while believers are told not to be deceived by it.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p179/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p179/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p179/r4.claim: Arabic prohibition grammatically targets the agent, as in the examples of telling Mahmoud not to strike Khalid or Ibrahim not to travel.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p179/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p179/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p179/r5.claim: The author also cites the prohibition against one people mocking another, where the people are the grammatical agents being prohibited.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p179/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p179/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p179/r6.claim: He asks why the verse does not use the more natural direct wording, do not be distracted by wealth and children, before explaining the advantages of its shift.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p180/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p180/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p180/r1.claim: Addressing wealth and children as the targets of prohibition depicts God protecting the believer by stopping the causes from approaching and distracting him.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p180/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p180/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p180/r2.claim: The wording heightens the warning by depicting money and children as pursuing the believer and seeking to tempt him, so that prohibiting them cuts off the cause of distraction.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p180/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p180/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p180/r3.claim: Attributing distraction to wealth and children warns believers to stay alert before they are ensnared without noticing, like the warning not to let someone deceive you.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p180/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p180/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p180/r4.claim: The metaphor gives wealth deliberate, rational agency, as though it lays a trap to catch the believer.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p181/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p181/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p181/r1.claim: Repeating la before children makes clear that either wealth alone or children alone can distract; joining them under one la could imply only their combination is forbidden.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p181/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p181/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p181/r2.claim: Wealth comes first because pursuing and increasing it consumes much time and can keep someone away from family.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p181/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p181/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p181/r3.claim: Although children are more valuable than wealth, wealth comes first because this passage concerns distraction, and because the next verse similarly places charity before righteousness.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p181/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p181/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p181/r5.claim: The pairing of remembrance with righteousness is apt because someone distracted from obligations and remembering God is not among the righteous.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p182/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p182/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p182/r1.claim: Across Quranic pairings, wealth generally precedes children because it more often occupies people or invites display and boasting; he illustrates this with three passages.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p183/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p183/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p183/r1.claim: Saying whoever does this attributes the distraction to the person's own action and responsibility, affirming that he could turn away from it rather than being a passive victim.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p183/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p183/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p183/r2.claim: The imperfect verb signals a recurrent, ongoing pattern of distraction, which suits the daily repetition of worldly preoccupation.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p183/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p183/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p183/r3.claim: The ongoing form also avoids suggesting that one isolated distraction earns this immense loss; repeated conduct better fits the emphatic nominal verdict.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p183/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p183/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p183/r4.claim: Loss is the fitting outcome because the distracted person seeks profit and growth for wealth, yet trades what is great and lasting for what is base and fleeting.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p184/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p184/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p184/r1.claim: The demonstrative, separating pronoun, and definite losers together restrict and intensify the verdict: these people are the true and fullest losers, rather than merely sharing some loss.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p184/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p184/r2.speaker: الألوسي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p184/r2.claim: Al-Alusi notes the emphatic restriction created by the demonstrative, the repetition of predication, and the separating pronoun.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p184/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p184/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p184/r3.claim: Remembrance of God is broader than a single ritual such as prayer or jihad: it includes all obligations and inward, spoken, or heart-held remembrance, so the prohibition covers every deed done without God's presence.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p184/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p184/r4.speaker: الحسن
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p184/r4.claim: Al-Hasan is cited as saying that remembrance here encompasses all obligatory duties.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p282/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p282/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p282/r1.claim: The verse warns believers against letting wealth and children distract them from remembering God; whoever does so incurs great loss.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p283/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p283/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p283/r1.claim: Directly addressing wealth protects believers by forbidding the cause of distraction before it can affect them, and makes the warning more forceful.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p283/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p283/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p283/r2.claim: The metaphor portrays wealth and children as plotting to ensnare believers, warning them to stay alert rather than become distracted without agency.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p283/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p283/r3.speaker: روح المعاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p283/r3.claim: Ruh al-Ma'ani says the prohibition is really directed at people, but addresses wealth because it strongly causes and contributes to distraction.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p283/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p283/r4.speaker: البيضاوي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p283/r4.claim: Al-Baydawi explains that directing the prohibition toward wealth and its like is for emphasis.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p283/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p283/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p283/r5.claim: Repeating la before children shows that either wealth or children can distract alone; without it, the wording could imply that only their combination is prohibited.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p284/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p284/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p284/r1.claim: Wealth precedes children because managing and growing it consumes time and can distract a person from family; children are more valuable since wealth serves them and is left to them.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p284/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p284/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p284/r2.claim: The sequence mirrors the next verse: after forbidding distraction by wealth, the text puts charity first, since charity releases wealth from hand and heart; remembrance then corresponds to becoming righteous.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p284/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p284/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p284/r3.claim: The Quran generally puts wealth before children when distraction, adornment, or boasting is in view, but puts loved relatives first in the love-focused list in Tawbah.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p285/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p285/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p285/r1.claim: In Tawbah, relatives precede wealth because the context is love: close family together are dearer than money, which people spend on them and leave to them.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p285/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p285/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p285/r2.claim: Saying whoever does that assigns the action to the person, affirming that distraction is within one's control and that one is responsible for it.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p285/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p285/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p285/r3.claim: The present tense yaf'al signals the repeated, ongoing distraction that occurs day after day, unlike a one-time past action.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p286/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p286/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p286/r1.claim: A past verb might suggest that even one occurrence brings the stated loss; the categorical nominal ending better fits recurring distraction and lasting loss.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p286/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p286/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p286/r2.claim: Calling them the losers fits people who seek profit through wealth: distraction is actually a loss, trading the lasting great for the trivial and perishable.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p286/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p286/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p286/r3.claim: The demonstrative, separating pronoun, and definite losers restrict and intensify the judgment: these people are the true and most complete losers.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p286/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p286/r4.speaker: روح المعاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p286/r4.claim: Ruh al-Ma'ani likewise reads the demonstrative, restriction, repeated predication, and separating pronoun as emphatic.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p286/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p286/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p286/r5.claim: Remembering God is chosen because it encompasses every duty: worship is done for God through inward or spoken remembrance, including prayer, praise, and supplication.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p286/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p286/r6.speaker: الحسن
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p286/r6.claim: Hasan glosses remembering God here as all the religious obligations.

STUDYQURAN:63:9/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:63:9/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:63:9/r1.claim: Wealth and children do not bring people near to God apart from faith and righteous action; enduring righteous deeds are better than worldly adornments.

STUDYQURAN:63:9/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:63:9/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:63:9/r2.claim: On Judgment Day, wealth and children avail nothing except for the one who comes to God with a sound heart.

STUDYQURAN:63:9/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:63:9/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:63:9/r3.claim: Those who deal justly with worldly possessions and responsibilities are rewarded, while wealth and children cannot protect disbelievers from God.

STUDYQURAN:63:9/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:63:9/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:63:9/r4.claim: The Quran warns that God may punish disbelievers through their wealth and children in this life, and cites other warnings about worldly attachments.

STUDYQURAN:63:9/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:63:9/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:63:9/r5.claim: “Remembrance of God” can mean the practice of dhikr, remembrance of God.

STUDYQURAN:63:9/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:63:9/r6.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:63:9/r6.claim: An alternative rendering is “the reminder of God,” referring to the Quran because Reminder is one of the Quran’s names.
